Translators and interpreters must be adequately credentialed and adequately represent the preferred languages spoken by residents of the county requesting services. Employees should work with their supervisors, department heads, elected officials, human resources and/or the comptrollers office as necessary to obtain services for an approved translation service provider. While Charlie attempted access to the interior of the structure, Jesse carried a 24’ ladder around to the C side of the structure locating the victim on the balcony. He placed the ladder and even utilized a rock to stabilize it due to the angle. He then ascended the ladder and assisted the resident over the railing and down to safety. Without his efforts, the outcome could have been fatal.

source_snippets: X. Briefing from the Chair and Executive Director Chair Berry expressed appreciation for everyone’s comments and impressed that industry suggestions are taken seriously. He said decisions on anything that may impact cost or ability to drive business is greatly considered. He was glad to attend the Cannabis Regulation Association conference and hear what is happening in the industry around the nation and he learned about good practices and the challenges. Chair Berry opined that discussion and debate between industry and regulators is necessary and he is impressed by Nevada. Discussion and Possible Action to Approve a 2027 Legislative Session Bill Draft Request from the Carson City School District to eliminate the Nevada Education Performance Framework (NEPF) At the August 11, 2026 meeting of the Board of Trustees, Mr. Feuling, Mr. Bringhurst, and Mr. Carstens presented on a possible Bill Draft Request (BDR) for the 2027 Session of the Nevada Legislature. The BDR would eliminate the Nevada Educator Performance Framework as the statewide evaluation system for teachers and administrators and return that authority to local school districts. Mr. Feuling has completed the required form to submit before the September 1, 2026 deadline. A copy of the required form is included in board packets. Staff recommends approval.

Parents play an integral role in assisting student learning: Educators recognize and acknowledge parents’ roles as the integral and primary facilitator of their children’s education. Research demonstrates that student achievement increases when parents are actively involved in the learning process. To protect this integral role, the District guarantees parents the right to proactive, advance notice and an accessible opt-out accommodation for instructional materials or supplemental curricula that substantially intersect with a family’s religious development, moral beliefs, or sensitive personal topics, with alternative academic assignments provided without penalty.

1. Who is eligible to request an exemption from the physical education requirement? A student may request an exemption if they meet one of the following conditions: • A physical or mental condition supported by a physician’s statement. • A religious belief supported by a parent or guardian’s statement. • Enrollment in Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) or a course of study in military science. • Enrollment in the school’s marching band. • Participate in interscholastic athletics, on a drill team, in a dance group, or on a cheerleading squad sponsored by the school, and complete the activity in good standing. • Actively participate in an approved competitive club or individual sport/activity for at least 120 hours outside the school day.

source_snippets: 1. FOR DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ACTION: REVIEW ANALYSIS OF AIRPORT STAFFING NEEDS AND APPROVE ADDITIONAL STAFF POSITION OF ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT. (C. Jenkins) Staff Summary: Carson City Airport is in a period of growth with new hangar construction, new ground leases, and increased interest in more development. The airport manager must regularly push aside activities that support this growth to complete competing priority items related to airport safety, general administrative tasks, service to local government agencies, and federal grant assurance compliance. Current and projected airport growth supports hiring additional staff to provide the best possible service to the community. Staff recommends adding an Administrative Assistant position to address this need.

source_snippets: A. Overbroad Definition of Non-Protected Speech (Regulation 4392, Section II.B) • The Policy Language: CCSD Regulation 4392 states: "when District employees engage in speech that arises directly from their work, the speech is not protected... speech is considered to arise from an employee's work when the speech concerns a subject matter that primarily involves the employee's job or duties." It further claims that "specific issues, concerns, or grievances regarding a District employee's work are not considered matters of public concern." • The Violation: This definition overreaches Garcetti v. Ceballos. Garcetti applies strictly to speech made pursuant to official job duties (e.g., writing an official internal memo), NOT speech about a workplace topic made in an employee's private capacity. Declaring that anything "involving" a job cannot be a matter of public concern unconstitutionall...

source_snippets: 5. Approved-UNR – Program Proposal, B.S. Aerospace Engineering – The Committee recommended approval of a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Aerospace Engineering aimed to address the growing demand for aerospace professionals in Nevada, filling a critical gap in workforce development that has arisen due to the diversification of Nevada’s economy. Students will learn about materials used to create lightweight structures, propulsion systems that launch vehicles and sustain flight, aerodynamics of aircraft, and control systems that must respond to unpredictable outside forces. The program will leverage the Gillemot Gift to enhance research capabilities, foster industry partnerships, and provide high-quality education. (Ref. ARSA-5 on file in the Board Office)

Information Only – First Quarter Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Athletics Financial Report, UNLV, UNR, CSN, and TMCC – (Continued) Regent Goodman asked how the Athletic Department got to a $27 million deficit. UNLV Vice President Wyman stated there was a policy change associated with the reporting of deficit on accounts. They previously did not have to report on certain capital projects associated with gift revenue at the account level. The second part was faulty assumptions. The previous Chief Financial Officer worked with the Athletic Department to develop a model for the annual budget which had some anticipations for unrestricted gift-giving, but the Department received the funds via restricted gift-giving. Because UNLV had to pivot from unrestricted to restricted, that drove the deficit.

source_snippets: 2. Approved – Annual Report – (Continued) In response to a question from Regent Brown related to their use of a different accounting method, WNC Foundation Finance Chair Scott Fields responded that based on the accounting method used they do not track restricted funds in the same way that other entities in NSHE do. The WNC Foundation has adopted GASB Statement No 33 which does not present that type of information in the financials. But if she was looking for something comparable, he referred her to the unexpended liability section on the balance sheet. Dr. Dana Ryan, Vice President of Academic and Student Affairs, WNC, reported a program review identified the three programs as terminal, non-transferrable, and no longer aligned with current workforce expectations. Dr. Ryan noted that the A.A.S. pathway in these areas has become less effective for students, as most related careers require a baccalaureate degree or higher for entry. All currently enrolled students will be supported through individualized advising plans to ensure program completion and applicable transitions over the next six years, until the programs phase out. source_snippets: 3. Spot Zoning Inconsistencies in the Downtown Mixed Use Expansion If Downtown Mixed Use (DTMU) zoning is planned to extend north to Winnie Lane, there must be consistent application. As currently proposed, John and Corbett Streets are included in the DTMU designation, yet Rice Street—directly between them—is completely excluded without any stated reason. I have raised this issue multiple times at Master Plan review meetings and through the online portal and have yet to receive any explanation. This kind of arbitrary spot zoning raises serious concerns about transparency and fairness in how zoning boundaries are being drawn. Residents deserve consistent and accountable planning—not piecemeal decisions that affect property values and neighborhood character without public justification.

It occurs in approximately 16 populations primarily located on the margins of these valleys, within sagebrush scrub habitat. It flowers in April to May each year and responds strongly to the preceding winter’s precipitation: in wet years there may be very robust blooms, while in drought years it may not flower at all. Endemic to this corner of the western Great Basin, it was described as a distinct taxon in 2012. source_snippets: 6. Consideration of Subcommittee Name Revision to Reflect Codified Statutory Reference (Information, Discussion, and for Possible Action) Chair Braxton introduced the idea of updating the subcommittee’s name to reflect the codified statute now guiding its work, rather than referencing the original Assembly Bill (AB 469). Deputy Superintendent Ford recommended shortening the name to simply reflect "NRS 388G" instead of listing the full statute range, as the provisions may be amended in the future. After brief discussion, the members agreed to rename the subcommittee the NRS 388G Subcommittee to align with current statutory language and to clarify its purpose. Motion to change the name of the AB 469 Subcommittee to the NRS 388G Subcommittee. Motion by Chair Braxton, seconded by Member Hudson. Motion passed unanimously.

source_snippets: V. Consideration of License Agreements A. Commerce Park Medical RD264 LLC (RD264), Main Street Tenant LLC, and Alpine Building LLC – Lease Agreement David Staley, Chief of Investigation gave a briefing on item 5A. Item Number 5, which consists of one lease agreement, item A1, is a lease agreement between Main Street Tenant LLC, a subsidiary of CPCM. Holding LLC and Alpine Building LLC. An isolated artifact is considered single and unassociated when separated by 30 meters or more from any other artifact. For example, two flakes of the same or different raw material separated by 29 meters would be documented as a site. Ten pieces of glass from a single bottle spread across 31 meters would be an isolate. Isolates are not recorded on a site form, but are listed in a table designated by number, description, and location.

source_snippets: I. Isolated artifacts: An isolated artifact is defined herein as a single artifact or pieces from a single artifact, i.e., 10 pieces of glass from a single bottle. An isolated artifact is considered single and unassociated when separated by 30 meters or more from any other artifact. For example, two flakes of the same or different raw material separated by 29 meters would be documented as a site. Ten pieces of glass from a single bottle spread across 31 meters would be an isolate. Isolates are not recorded on a site form, but are listed in a table designated by number, description, and location.

Isolated features that have potential data (fire hearth) must be recorded as a site and evaluated for eligibility.

This designation is intended to create opportunities for a mix of uses in a concentrated setting that encourages a “one-stop shop” setting. The Master Plan discusses that when the Community /Regional Commercial land use abuts lower intensity land uses, buffering and transition space should be provided to reduce visual and noise impacts. The subject site serves as a transition from the large lot residential zoned properties to the east and the higher intensity uses to the west. The proposed use is consistent with this land use designation. As proposed, and with recommended conditions, the proposal is consistent with the adopted Master Plan and Elements.
